products.description:
This tool functions as a personal soundscape generator, creating single ambient audio experiences tailored to your specific prompts. By leveraging a Large Language Model (LLM), it intelligently selects and mixes sounds from a library to produce a unique MP3 file that matches the mood or environment you describe.

(Note: To build longer evolving sound journeys, use the tool 'ambient sound journey composer', which uses the present tool under the hood.)

### How to Use the Tool:

This tool offers a straightforward, step-by-step process for creating your ideal ambient soundscape:

1.  **Download the Sound Library**: Before you can generate any soundscapes, you must first download the necessary audio assets. To do this, simply run the tool with the `download_assets` option set to `True`. This will fetch the default sound library from a GitHub repository and store it on your local machine. The tool supports .mp3 and .wav sound files.

2.  **Customize with Your Own Sounds (Optional)**: You have the creative freedom to expand the sound library. To add your own audio, just place any MP3 or WAV files into the designated `assets_folder`. You can also create subfolders to organize your sounds by category. For best results, use only a 2 level depth (categories, subcategories, no more). The tool will automatically detect and integrate these new files, making them available for your soundscapes.

3.  **Generate Your Soundscape**: Once your sound library is ready, you can start creating. Provide a descriptive `prompt` detailing the type of ambient sound you want (e.g., "a peaceful forest with a gentle stream and distant birds"). The tool will then generate a custom MP3 file based on your description.

4.  **Explore Your Sound Options (Optional)**: If you're unsure what sounds are available or want to get ideas for your prompts, you can set the `show_available_sounds` option to `True`. This will provide a complete list of all the sounds in your library, including any you've added yourself, without generating an audio file.
products.name: Ambient Sound Composer

products.author: hanzo.ai
products.description:
This tool crafts custom, long-form evolving ambient soundscapes from a simple text description. It intelligently orchestrates a detailed composition plan, breaking the total duration into smaller, evolving segments. It then generates each segment individually, ensuring smooth, gradual transitions before seamlessly stitching them into a single, continuous MP3 audio file. It relies on local sound assets.

It's perfect for creating background audio for focus, relaxation, or storytelling that evolves over time.

This tool relies on the 'ambient sound composer' tool, which you can configure first.

### How to Use It

To create your soundscape, simply write a descriptive `request` outlining the audio journey you envision. Be as detailed as you would like, or vague for more random outputs. You can define the `total_duration_minutes`, suggest a number of `segments` to guide the pacing, and provide a custom `output_filename` for the final MP3. These core inputs give you direct control over the final audio composition.

For more insight, you can use several optional toggles. Set `show_available_sounds` to `true` to get a list of all sound building blocks without generating audio. To see the AI's step-by-step "recipe" for your track, enable `show_composition_plan`. Finally, if you wish to examine the individual audio clips used, you can choose to `keep_intermediate_files` rather than having them automatically deleted.
products.name: Ambient Sound Journey Composer

products.author: hanzo.ai
products.description:
This tool reads an input CSV file, processes specified columns and combine them according to a user-defined prompt using an LLM, and adds the results to a new column in the output CSV. It supports error handling, retries, skips rows with empty cells, and provides detailed processing statistics. The output can either override the input file, or be saved to a new CSV file with a timestamp (e.g., "input_processed_20250421_143022.csv") and placed in the same folder as the input CSV.

How to Use :

1. Configure Defaults : Set default CSV parameters : delimiter (e.g., ';'), encoding (e.g., 'utf-8'), quotechar (e.g., '"'), max LLM retries (e.g., 2), and default output behavior ('new_file' or 'override').

2. Prepare Input CSV file : Use an existing CSV file with the data to process.

3. Provide a prompt with {} placeholders matching CSV column names (e.g., "Summarize this product description in one sentence : {Description}.", "Population of {City} in {Date}, just write the number").

4. Specify New Column Name : Set the name for the new column to store LLM results (e.g., "Summary", "Population_Size").

5. Provide Optional Data Description : Include a brief context about the data to guide the LLM (e.g., "Product descriptions from a retail dataset.").

6. Set Custom CSV Parameters (Optional) : Customize delimiter, encoding, or quotechar to match the input CSV ; defaults from configuration apply if not specified.

7. Choose Output Behavior (Optional) : Select 'new_file' for a new output file or 'override' to replace the input file; defaults to configuration if not set.

8. Run the Tool : Execute with the provided inputs.

9. Review Summary : Check the output message for stats (e.g., total rows, processed rows, empty cell errors, LLM errors) and the output CSV path.

10. Verify Output CSV file : Inspect the resulting CSV with the new column containing LLM-processed data.

High LLM Usage Warning : This tool makes an LLM call for each processed row, which may result in significant usage.
products.name: CSV column AI combinator

products.description:

It includes error handling, retries, skips empty values, and provides a summary of the processing results.

The output can either override the input file, or be saved to a new CSV file with a timestamp (e.g., "input_processed_20250421_143022.csv") and placed in the same folder as the input CSV.

How to Use :

0. In configuration, set default CSV parameters : delimiter (e.g., ';'), encoding (e.g., 'utf-8'), and quotechar (e.g., '"') ; and set the max number of retries for the LLM categorization (e.g., 2), and the default output behavior ('new_file' or 'override').

1. Prepare an Input CSV File : Create or use an existing CSV file containing the data you want to categorize.

2. Define Categories : Provide a comma-separated string of categories (e.g., "Electronics, Clothing, Home Goods, Toys, Other").

3. Specify the Column to Categorize : Indicate the column name in the CSV that contains the data to be categorized (e.g., "Description").

4. Choose a New Column Name : Set the name for the new column that will store the categorization results (e.g., "Category").

5. Provide an Optional Data Description : Add a brief description of the data to assist the LLM in understanding the context (e.g., "Product descriptions from an e-commerce store.").

6. Set Custom CSV Parameters (Optional), make sure they match the parameters of the input CSV file : Customize the delimiter (e.g., ";"), encoding (e.g., "utf-8"), or quote character (e.g., '"') if needed; otherwise, defaults from configuration will be applied.

7. Choose Output Behavior (Optional): Select 'new_file' for a new output file or 'override' to replace the input file; defaults to configuration if not set.

8. Run the Tool : Execute the tool with the provided inputs.

9. Check the Summary : After processing, review the summary message for statistics (e.g., total rows, categorized rows, skipped rows, errors) and the path to the output CSV file.

10. Check the output CSV file with the categorization.

High LLM usage warning : this tool creates a LLM call for each cell to process.
products.name: CSV Column Categorizer

products.author: hanzo.ai
products.description:
Ingests local directories or remote GitHub repositories and consolidates their contents into a single, structured text file, optimized for LLM analysis.

Key Features:

*   Dual Source Ingestion: Processes code from either a local file path or a direct GitHub repository URL.
*   Structured Output: Generates a clean document containing a summary, a visual directory tree, and the full content of each included file.
*   Granular Content Filtering: Provides robust control over what gets included, with sensible defaults for:
    *   Ignoring common directories (`.git`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, etc.).
    *   Ignoring binary and non-text file extensions (`.pyc`, `.png`, `.pdf`, etc.).
    *   Including only recognized code-like files (`.py`, `.js`, `.yml`, `.md`, etc.).
*   File Size Capping: Prevents overly large outputs by skipping the content of individual files that exceed a configurable size limit.
*   Flexible Export Formats: Outputs the final document as either Markdown (`.md`) for rich formatting or Plain Text (`.txt`) for maximum compatibility.
*   LLM-Ready Metrics: Reports the total token count (using `cl100k_base`) and final file size upon completion.

Notes:

*   Individual files larger than 100 KB are skipped by default to manage output size. This limit is configurable via the `max_file_size_kb` input.
*   The tool recursively scans all subdirectories, building a complete map of the project structure while applying the filtering rules.
*   The `git` command-line tool must be installed and accessible in your system's PATH to process GitHub URLs.
products.name: Directory and Repo Ingestion

products.description:
This tool launches a specified application to open a designated file or directory.
You provide the path to the executable (e.g., 'notepad.exe', 'C:\Program Files\RStudio\rstudio.exe'), the path to the file or directory you want it to open (e.g., 'path_to\personal_notes.txt', 'path_to\R_project_directory'), and any optional additional command-line arguments.
The tool reports success, the process ID (PID), and the command executed.

Prompt Examples:

1. Open a text file with Notepad (Windows)

To open the text file C:\Users\YourUser\Documents\personal_notes.txt using notepad.exe:

executable_path: "notepad.exe"
file_to_open_path: "C:\\Users\\YourUser\\Documents\\personal_notes.txt"
additional_args: []

2. Open an R project directory with RStudio (Windows)

To open the R project located in the directory D:\Work\R_Projects\Customer_Churn_Analysis using a specific RStudio installation:

executable_path: "C:\\Program Files\\RStudio\\rstudio.exe"
file_to_open_path: "D:\\Work\\R_Projects\\Customer_Churn_Analysis"
additional_args: []

3. Open a document with LibreOffice Writer (Windows)

To open the document C:\Shared\TeamReports\Q3_Summary.docx using a specific LibreOffice Writer installation, perhaps with an argument to open it read-only (if supported, e.g., --view or similar, specific arguments depend on the application):

executable_path: "C:\\Program Files\\LibreOffice\\program\\swriter.exe"
file_to_open_path: "C:\\Shared\\TeamReports\\Q3_Summary.docx"
additional_args: ["--view"]
(Note: --view is an example; actual read-only flags vary by application. For simple opening, [] is fine.)

4. Open an image file with Microsoft Paint (Windows)

To open the image C:\MyPictures\Holiday\beach.jpg using mspaint.exe:

executable_path: "mspaint.exe"
file_to_open_path: "C:\\MyPictures\\Holiday\\beach.jpg"
additional_args: []

5. Open an R script with RStudio and additional options (assuming 'rstudio' is in PATH)

To open the R script /home/data_scientist/projects/my_analysis_v2.R using the rstudio command, without restoring the previous workspace or environment:

executable_path: "rstudio"
file_to_open_path: "/home/data_scientist/projects/my_analysis_v2.R"
additional_args: ["--no-restore-workspace", "--no-environ"]

products.author: hanzo.ai
products.description:
This tool manages text-based notes across multiple .txt files using natural language prompts.
It leverages an LLM to interpret user requests, identify which file to use, and perform actions : read, add, update, delete, move note to top or bottom.
It uses confirmation messages before modifying notes.

How to Use:

1. Set up multiple .txt files by topic with short clear distinct names, and add their path to file paths in configuration.

2. In configuration, also pick which note file to use as default.

3. Type a request in the prompt input. Make it clear which note file to use, and which action to perform.

4. Confirm actions via GUI dialogs when required.

Example Prompts:

- "Personal notes, add birthday party is at 6 pm on Wednesday."

- "What's the most urgent in my work notes?"

- "Update family notes, bike is better gift idea for brother"

- "Delete word notes, we're good with all clients calls " → Removes specified note.

- "Move exercise plan to top of personal notes" → Reorganizes note to top.

- "Open family notes" → Opens file in default .txt editor.

Additionally, the tool can also use the content from an image uploaded in the chat to interact with the notes.

To note, within each file, this tool considers that each distinct paragrah is a different note (uses "\n\n" as separator).
products.name: Note Manager
